latest.title: Hussar EP513 Pre-Drill Site Works Update
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 2728Q
Georgina Energy PLC
12 August 2026
12th August 2026
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT RELATES TO THE DISCLOSURE OF INFORMATION THAT QUALIFIED OR MAY HAVE QUALIFIED AS INSIDE INFORMATION WITHIN THE MEANING OF (A) ARTICLE 7(1) OF UK MAR IN SO FAR AS IT RELATES TO ORDINARY SHARES ISSUED BY GEORGINA ENERGY PLC
Georgina Energy plc
("Georgina", "Georgina Energy" or the "Company")
Hussar EP513 Pre-Drill Site Works Update
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, confirms that civil engineering contractors are currently completing the pre-drill site works, including water well drilling and conductor pipe drilling required for the planned Q3 Hussar drilling program. These works, including site and camp preparation, represent a key step towards mobilisation of the contracted Ensign 970 drill rig to enable the testing of this exciting prospect, which has 300 km² of areal closure and is one of the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbons prospects onshore Australia.
Highlights
·
September spud date for the Hussar well in Q3 2026 remains on target.
·
Water well drilling has commenced to provide the rig water supply. This will be used for drilling fluid makeup water with a proportion being purified with Reverse Osmosis treatment for ablutions and cooking.
·
Following completion of the water well, the rig will move closer to the centre of the drilling pad to drill and set the 20 inch conductor pipe.
·
The civil engineers have advanced site works including the Turkey's Nest (a water storage pond) and the sump to contain drill cuttings and any excess drilling fluid.
·
The cellar, where the conductor pipe and well head will be set, will soon be dug ahead of conductor pipe drilling and cementing.
Water well drilling rig operating on site
Water well drilling in progress
Aerial view of the water well drill rig drilling on site
With 300 km² of areal closure, the Hussar prospect ranks among the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbon prospects onshore Australia that remains untested.
The Hussar EP513 prospect re-entry in Exploration Permit 513 in the Officer Basin in Western Australia is primarily targeting subsalt reservoir formations, including the Townsend Formation and fractured Neoproterozoic basement lithologies, for helium, hydrogen and natural gas and is planned to drill to a Total Depth of approximately 3,200m which may be extended depending on gas occurrences and reservoir quality. Globally, fractured basement reservoirs similar to that targeted in the Hussar Prospect, have proven to be prolific producers. The Bach Ho field in fractured basement offshore Vietnam for example, at its peak produced 1.6 BCFGE (billion cubic feet of gas equivalent) per day and has been in continuous production for over 40 years. (
https://www.saltworkconsultants.com/downloads/Bach_Ho_Cuong_Warren_09.pdf
)
A secondary target is the hydrocarbon gas potential in the Kanpa and Hussar formations overlying the primary subsalt targets. These formations have not been adequately tested to date but have shown excellent porosities and hydrocarbon shows during previous drilling.
The Hussar prospect has an Independent Geological Report dated 1st February 2026 by Competent Person Mr Maki Petkovski certifying unrisked SPE PRMS (the Society of Petroleum Engineers and Petroleum Resource Management Systems) net attributable 2U Prospective Resources of 283 BCF helium, 315 BCF hydrogen and 2.93 TCF of hydrocarbon gas.
Based on the pricing of Helium US$450/MCFG and Hydrogen US$2.65/kg and US$8/MCF for hydrocarbon gas, these volumes would equate to a total potential combined net attributable unrisked potential in-situ value of c.
US$152 billion.
These are estimates in-situ values from the AER (Australian Energy Regulator) and HNT (Helium Price Index) developed by the Company based on unrisked prospective resources; they exclude production, separation and transport-to-market costs, and there is no certainty that any part of these resources will be commercially recovered.
Further updates will follow as we progress towards the September spud date along with additional site photos which can be viewed by shareholders on the Georgina website.
Anthony Hamilton, Chief Executive Officer of Georgina Energy, commented:
"The progress being made on site is an important step mobilisation of the Ensign 970 drill rig and we remain on track for the planned September spud date of this exciting prospect . Hussar is a significant subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbon prospect, and we look forward to providing further updates as preparations advance."
ENDS

Notes to Editors
Georgina Energy aims to become a leading player in the global energy market and is focused on establishing itself among the top producers of helium and hydrogen worldwide. With a strategic approach and leveraging the experienced management team's expertise, Georgina Energy aims to capitalize on opportunities in these critical energy sectors.
Georgina Energy has two principal onshore interests held through its wholly owned Australian subsidiary, Westmarket O&G. The first, the Hussar Prospect is located in the Officer Basin in Western Australia and Westmarket O&G holds a 100% working interest in the exploration permit. The second, the EPA155 Mt Winter Prospect, is located in the Amadeus Basin in the Northern Territory, subject to completion of the Sale Agreement Georgina Energy will hold a 100% working interest.
With the resource potential of the EP513 Hussar and the EPA155 Mt Winter projects in line with market demand trends, Georgina Energy is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing gap between supply and demand for hydrogen, helium and gaseous hydrocarbons in Australia and globally.

company_30s.what_they_do: GEX is a specialist helium and natural‑gas exploration company. It owns and operates drilling rigs that search for helium‑rich pockets in the earth’s crust, often in the UK and Ireland. Once a deposit is found, the company plans to extract the gas and sell it to industrial users such as MRI manufacturers, aerospace firms and power utilities.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Helium is a scarce, high‑value resource that is critical for advanced imaging, space exploration and cryogenic technology. Natural gas remains a key transition fuel. GEX’s potential to tap into these markets gives it a niche that few competitors can match, especially if it can prove the presence of commercially viable helium reserves.
company_30s.current_state: The company is still in the exploration phase – no production yet – but it has been actively raising capital, paying down debt and moving drilling operations forward. It is trading at a very low price relative to the implied value of its assets, which suggests a steep discount for investors who can weather the next few months of volatility.

rns_narrative: The latest filings show a steady stream of capital‑raising activity: share awards, warrant exercise, an equity issue and a recent debt repayment. This indicates the company is actively managing its balance sheet to fund exploration.

Operationally, GEX is pushing forward with drilling: a new site works update, mobilisation of the Hussar EP513 rig, and the execution of a drill contract. These milestones signal that the company is moving from planning to execution.

Corporate governance is also in motion – the AGM result was recently announced and the company is preparing for its next funding round. Together these events paint a picture of a business that is surviving, adapting, and gearing up for the next phase of exploration.

crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls are pointing to the company’s helium upside and the potential to reach a £700m‑£1bn valuation once results come in. They see the current price as a bargain and anticipate a sharp rebound.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears flag the uncertainty of drilling outcomes and the risk that the company might not find a commercially viable deposit. They worry about cost overruns and the possibility of running out of cash if the first results are disappointing.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community is largely silent now, but a few bullish posts hint at a possible rebound once the first drilling data is released. The lack of heavy chatter means there is room for surprise if positive news arrives.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for GEX is flat, indicating no public interest spikes – a classic contrarian green light.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the Hussar EP513 drilling run and the release of the first helium measurement report.
Positive drilling results that confirm a commercially viable helium deposit.
Announcement of a new funding round or a strategic partnership that would provide additional capital.
A breakout above the recent swing low accompanied by a surge in trading volume.
expect_next.watch_for: Key signals to confirm the thesis are: a confirmed helium presence, a drilling success letter from the geologist, a clear statement from management about expected first‑production dates, and a spike in volume that shows new institutional interest.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early‑to‑mid phase of a deep‑crash recovery. APEX compression suggests that the price is still tightly packed and ready to spring. Expect the mean reversion to start once the first positive drilling data is publicised, likely within the next 6–12 months.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: GEX sits at a deep crash, so the upside is asymmetric. If the price climbs to 50% of its all‑time high – roughly four times the current level – that would be a 300‑400% gain.
